solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Card game with limits on pack, reportedly?

indicators.note: reportedly means as people say it, so we want a word that is heard rather than read

blocks.note: a picket is a stake that tethers an animal such as a pack horse, limiting where it can roam; a picket line also restrains a pack of workers

explanation.surface: A card game where only a limited part of the deck is used, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: PIQUET is commonly said like PICKET, so the spoken stake or barrier spells the game.
explanation.definitionFit: Piquet is an old two-player trick-taking game played with a reduced pack of thirty-two cards.

clue.text: Risky investment — not the first — embezzlement!

indicators.note: not the first means the opening letter is dropped

blocks.note: speculation is investing in the hope of gain at high risk

explanation.surface: A dodgy investment scheme turns out to be fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: Peculation is the formal word for misappropriating funds entrusted to one, the same offence as stealing from an employer.

clue.text: Phoney call from pond life?

blocks.note: first meaning: a fraud posing as a doctor
second meaning: the sound a duck makes

explanation.walkthrough: 'Phoney call' suggests a hoax phone call; split it into a fake and a duck's cry.
explanation.definitionFit: A quack is a charlatan pretending to medical skill, and also the noise ducks on a pond make.

clue.text: Recluse wound up watch in middle of week

indicators.note: wound up in a down clue suggests winding upwards, so the word is read from the bottom
in places the piece inside the following letters
the middle of a word is its central letters

blocks.note: the two central letters of week
a timer is a device for watching time

explanation.surface: A hermit winds his watch in the middle of the week.
explanation.definitionFit: An eremite is a Christian hermit, someone who lives alone in seclusion for religious reasons.

clue.text: As is surface of mirror, reflecting shops entered by minister

indicators.note: a reflection shows things back to front, so the letters are read the other way round
something entered by another has that other placed inside it

blocks.note: delis are delicatessen shops
Rev, short for Reverend, is a minister's title

explanation.surface: Describing a mirror's coating while an image of shops visited by a clergyman appears in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reflecting' fits the mirror picture so neatly that it reads as description, yet it is the instruction to read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Mirrors are made by coating glass with a thin metallic layer, so the backing surface is described as coated with that metal.

clue.text: Current transaction, visionary

blocks.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current
a deal is a business transaction

explanation.surface: A present-day business deal described as forward-looking.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal as an adjective means existing only in the imagination, perfect but not real, which is what visionary can mean.

clue.text: French nobleman failing to keep order, ending in defeat

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside
the ending of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: a vice is a moral failing
OM is the Order of Merit
the last letter of defeat

explanation.surface: A French aristocrat fails to keep order and ends up defeated.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicomte is the French rank equivalent to a viscount, a nobleman just below a count.

clue.text: Left at the crease doubled up, player upset about that

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word is read bottom to top
about means around, so one piece goes round the other

blocks.note: a gamer is someone who plays games
a batter at the crease is in, and doubled up means written twice

explanation.surface: A batsman left at the crease, doubled over, while an opposing player is upset.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the batsman at the crease is said to be in; 'that' points back to the doubled IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Remaining means still there after others have gone, which is the sense of left over.

clue.text: Portal with bar up, zero getting in

indicators.note: up in a down clue means read from the bottom, so the word goes backwards
getting in means entering, so one letter goes inside

blocks.note: a rod is a bar
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: An entrance with its bar raised and nobody coming through.
explanation.definitionFit: A portal is a grand entrance or doorway, so the everyday word is the hinged barrier to a room.

clue.text: Enthusiastic volunteer having to improve before grammar lesson?

definitions.text: having to improve before grammar lesson?
definitions.note: a verb phrase, read as ungrammatical speech

blocks.note: first meaning: a well-meaning person eager to help others

blocks.clueFragment: having to improve before grammar lesson?
blocks.note: second meaning: someone who has not yet learned grammar might say they must 'do' better with a wrongly formed comparative

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the joke: before a grammar lesson someone might form the comparative of good wrongly, as GOODER.
explanation.definitionFit: A do-gooder is someone keen on charitable work, often used of an earnest or interfering volunteer.

clue.text: Companion taking time out from first part of novel?

indicators.note: taking something out means removing it, and time stands for one letter to drop

blocks.note: a novel's opening section is chapter one
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A companion book seems to take a break from the opening of a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the T from CHAPTER ONE to leave CHAPERONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaperone is a person who accompanies and supervises someone, especially a young woman at social events, acting as an escort.

clue.text: Bill’s partner visited by doctor in group

indicators.note: a place visited by someone has that visitor inside it

blocks.note: the phrase bill and coo pairs these words as lovers' billing and cooing
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: Bill's partner receives a visit from a doctor while out with a group of friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name, but it is the bird's beak in the idiom 'bill and coo'.
explanation.definitionFit: A combo is an informal name for a small band of musicians, especially in jazz, so it is a musical ensemble.

clue.text: Hobson’s choice — with only sugar cubes?

blocks.note: first meaning: a choice with only one real option, take it or leave it
second meaning: a whimsical tea order, where the drinker may prefer it or have it sweetened with cubes

explanation.walkthrough: Hobson was a Cambridge stable keeper who offered customers the horse nearest the door or none. The second half reads the idiom literally: lumps are sugar cubes.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means accept the situation because there is no alternative, exactly what a forced single option offers.

clue.text: Aggressive and popular solver’s champion, keeping fine

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so a letter is placed within the last piece

blocks.note: in means fashionable or popular
the clue addresses the solver as you, so the solver's is your
an ace is an expert or champion
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A combative but popular puzzle champion holding on to a fine.
explanation.definitionFit: In-your-face describes blatantly confrontational behaviour, bold and provocative rather than restrained.

clue.text: Heading past it, leaseholder’s housing

indicators.note: housing means holding inside, so the answer sits within the neighbouring words

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of past, all of it and the start of leaseholder's

explanation.surface: A leaseholder getting on in years heads for the home they own.
explanation.definitionFit: A title is the heading printed at the top of a chapter, article or document, naming its subject.

clue.text: At this point, Father carried by boy out of that place

indicators.note: carried by means held within, so the earlier words go inside the next

blocks.note: Tom is a boy's name
here means at this place
Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title

explanation.surface: At this moment a priest is carried off by a boy from somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Therefrom is a formal adverb meaning from that thing or location, used in legal and old-fashioned writing.

clue.text: Flower put on garlands also by priest

indicators.note: a garland wraps around something, so one word encircles the others

blocks.note: to don clothes is to put them on
and adds something, like also
Eli is the priest in the Book of Samuel; by places him next to the previous word

explanation.surface: A flower is placed on garlands, and a priest adds another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Garlands' looks like a noun for flowers, but it is a verb meaning encircles.
explanation.definitionFit: The dandelion is a common yellow-flowered weed whose seed head becomes a fluffy clock.

clue.text: Piece hot off the press, Times cryptic

indicators.note: cryptic means puzzling and disguised, so the letters are scrambled out of recognition

blocks.note: freshly printed means new
the letters of times rearranged

explanation.surface: A news story fresh from the printers, alongside this very puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue appears in The Times, so the setter is talking about their own cryptic.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece in journalism is an article, and a news item is one such report printed in a paper.

clue.text: How to contain runs after evident result of fielding error

indicators.note: to contain is to hold something within, so one piece goes inside another
after puts the first piece behind the one named next

blocks.note: overt means plain to see
taken as written
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A cricket question: how to limit runs after an obvious misfield.
explanation.walkthrough: 'How' looks like the start of a question but is taken literally as letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket an overthrow is a wild return from a fielder that misses the stumps, letting the batsmen take extra runs.

clue.text: Fuel in test that’s explosive, ladies and gentlemen

indicators.note: an explosion scatters things, so the letters are blown into a new order
in places the first piece inside the second

blocks.note: oil is a fuel
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fuel trial that blows up, announced to an audience of ladies and gentlemen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ladies and gentlemen' looks like a greeting, but it means the signs on public conveniences.
explanation.definitionFit: Ladies and gentlemen are the signs on public restrooms, so together they name the conveniences.

clue.text: Fighting earlier involving leaders in Glorious Revolution

indicators.note: involving means taking something in, so letters go inside another word
leaders are the front runners, so the opening letter of each following word is used

blocks.note: ago means in the past
the first letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Violent fighting from history, led by figures in the Glorious Revolution of 1688.
explanation.walkthrough: The Glorious Revolution was the 1688 overthrow of James II in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggro is British slang for aggressive trouble or violent behaviour, shortened from aggravation.

clue.text: Tanks in piazza stripped, one occupying area after evacuation

indicators.note: stripped means its outer layer taken off, so the first and last letters go
occupying means sitting inside, so these pieces go within the next
evacuated means emptied, so only the outside letters stay

blocks.note: a piazza is a square; stripped of its outer letters it leaves the middle
I is the Roman numeral one
the outer letters of area

explanation.surface: Fish tanks in a cleared Italian square, one put in place after the area was evacuated.
explanation.walkthrough: A piazza is an Italian public square, giving SQUARE before stripping.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquaria is a plural of aquarium, the glass tanks used to keep fish and other water creatures.

clue.text: Note I tremble after death march’s beginning

indicators.note: after puts the preceding pieces behind the ones named next
the beginning of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: demise means death
the first letter of march
taken as written
to quaver is to shake or tremble

explanation.surface: Someone trembles after the opening of a funeral march.
explanation.walkthrough: Note how 'quaver' is itself a musical note, which helps once the long word appears.
explanation.definitionFit: A demisemiquaver is a very short musical note, a thirty-second note, worth one eighth of a crotchet.

clue.text: Hungry vampire, Dracula biting the vicar last of all

indicators.note: last of all asks for the final letter of every word named

blocks.note: the final letter of each of the five words

explanation.surface: A ravenous vampire, Count Dracula, sinks his teeth into the vicar.
explanation.definitionFit: Eager means keenly wanting something, as in eager for food, so it can stand for hungry.

clue.text: House where burglar, say, drops in?

indicators.note: to drop something is to let it fall away, so the named letters are removed

blocks.note: a burglar is an example of a criminal
taken as written

explanation.surface: A house where a burglar pops in unexpectedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drops in' reads as visiting, but it means dropping the letters IN from VILLAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A villa is a large country or seaside residence, a type of dwelling.

clue.text: Bad to be wrongly directed

indicators.note: pointed the wrong way means turned round, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: to live is to be, to exist

explanation.surface: Being misguided is a bad thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Evil means morally wicked, the strongest sense of wrong or harmful conduct.

clue.text: Poetry in very old language

blocks.note: V is the abbreviation for very
Erse is an old name for Scottish or Irish Gaelic

explanation.surface: Poetry written in a very old tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Verse is writing arranged in metrical lines, the general term for poetic composition.

clue.text: Blunder in Caribbean location not initiated by an irregular soldier

indicators.note: not initiated by means the opening is missing, and it names the opening letters to remove
in places the first piece inside the second

blocks.note: to err is to make a mistake
Anguilla is an island territory in the Caribbean

explanation.surface: A rebel fighter makes a blunder somewhere in the Caribbean.
explanation.walkthrough: Anguilla is a small British territory in the eastern Caribbean; 'by an' reads as part of the soldier phrase but names the letters to cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A guerrilla is a member of a small independent fighting band, not part of a regular army.

clue.text: Monk’s home brewing Mary’s ale

indicators.note: brewing stirs ingredients together into something new, so the letters are mixed

blocks.note: the letters of the two words, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A monastery where Mary's beer is brewed, as monks are known to do.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamasery is a monastery of lamas, the monks of Tibetan Buddhism.

clue.text: Music genre for example, a type of jazz that’s retro

indicators.note: retro means looking backwards, so everything before it is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: e.g. abbreviates for example
taken as written
rag, short for ragtime, is an early jazz style

explanation.surface: A music style, for instance an old-fashioned kind of jazz.
explanation.definitionFit: Garage is a style of electronic dance music that grew from house music in the 1990s, especially in the UK.
